As of 325 PM EDT Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Breezy and mostly sunny fall-like Monday for 
most. Breezy NNE winds continue through the middle of the week, 
with potentially unsettled conditions along the immediate coast.

Latest wx analysis shows strong ~1038mb high pressure over the area 
this afternoon. After a cool start this morning, temperatures have 
risen to the upper 50s to lower 60s across the area, despite an 
abundance of sunshine for most. High clouds have developed over SE 
VA/NE NC, from low pressure offshore. Tonight, temperatures will be 
cool again with lows in the upper 30s in the piedmont, lower 40s 
inland, and low to mid 50s along the coast. Similar to this morning, 
frost formations is not expected due to a light breeze. 

A mid/upper level trough has become closed off this afternoon, 
developing a Nor'easter that will meander offshore. The hi-res and 
global models have came into better agreement with the 12z model 
runs showing the low strengthening, but staying further offshore. 
Some outer rain bands may reach coastal portions of the area, but 
PoPs have decreased as the track has moved further away. There is 
now only 15-30% PoP along SE VA/NE NC on Monday. With the low 
lingering offshore and high pressure to our north, persistent breezy 
conditions inland and prolonged windy conditions are expected along 
the immediate coast. N-NE gusts will average 20 to 25 mph inland and 
30 to 45+ mph along the coast, highest over the Virginia Capes south 
to the NC Northern Outer Banks. A Wind Advisory is in effect for 
Eastern Currituck county and the City of Virginia Beach through 
Monday night, as this is where gusts will be highest. There is still 
some uncertainty on how long the low lingers offshore and the 
potential track, but most models indicate the low slowly shifting 
east-northeast further out to sea by midweek. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...A long-duration coastal flood event is 
expected. Coastal Flood Watches are in effect from Monday 
through early Wednesday morning across the lower Chesapeake Bay,
lower James River, and the Atlantic coast.

Model guidance continue to exhibit spread regarding a Nor'easter
lingering offshore early this week with respect to intensity 
and placement, particularly beyond Tuesday. With the cutoff low 
detached from the primary jet stream and lacking an upstream 
kicker trough, probabilistic ensembles favor a system meandering
offshore through midweek. Gusty N-NE winds will drive building 
tidal anomalies over the next few days.

Prolonged onshore flow will drive anomalies to 1 to 3 feet 
above normal astronomical tide. Fortunately, the region is 
currently in an astronomical neap tide cycle, which will help to
mitigate peak water levels. Even so, widespread minor to 
moderate coastal flooding is expected during high tides into the
middle of the week. If the low strengthens or edges closer to 
the coast, localized major flooding cannot be ruled out, though 
most guidance continues to trend "lower" toward high-end minor 
to moderate thresholds. Additionally, the latest model guidance
shows tidal levels continuing to gradually increase into Wed
with gradually higher tidal levels each day. For now, have
issued a Coastal Flood Advisory along the lower James River as
well as Virginia Beach and eastern Currituck. While more
marginal than yesterday's high tide, nuisance to minor coastal
flooding is expected with this afternoon's high tide across this
region. Not every location will reach minor flood stage.
However, with Smithfield and Fort Monroe favored to reach minor
flood stage as well as factoring in that a few non-forecast 
sites around Norfolk and Virginia Beach are trending higher than
nearby TWL sites and will likely reach minor flood stage, have 
gone ahead and included that whole region for the advisory.
Otherwise, have extended the Coastal Flood Watch through early 
Wed morning given the gradually increasing tides.

Coastal Flood Watches and Advisories are now in effect from 
Monday through early Wednesday morning across the lower
